🍍 When to plant pineapple in Nigeria

Also called Ọ̀pẹ òyìnbó (Yoruba) and Abarba (Hausa).

Quick answer: Plant pineapple in Nigeria from March to May and harvest from November to April. Suckers are planted early in the rains; first fruits come 18–24 months later. Most fruit is sold in the dry season.

PlantMarch to May
HarvestNovember to April
Grows inSouth-West, South-South, South-East and North-Central
TypeFruits

About pineapple

Edo and Ogun states are known for large pineapple farms.

How to plant pineapple well

Plant healthy suckers in well-drained soil.

Suckers are planted early in the rains; first fruits come 18–24 months later. Most fruit is sold in the dry season.

Diseases and pests of pineapple

  • Mealybug wiltPlant clean suckers and control the ants that carry mealybugs.
  • Heart rotPlant on well-drained land and avoid injuring plants.

Best states for pineapple

Edo · Ogun · Osun · Oyo · Delta · Cross River · Lagos · Kwara

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant pineapple in Nigeria?

Plant pineapple in Nigeria from March to May and harvest from November to April. Suckers are planted early in the rains; first fruits come 18–24 months later. Most fruit is sold in the dry season.

What is pineapple called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Pineapple is called Ọ̀pẹ òyìnbó (Yoruba) and Abarba (Hausa).

When is pineapple harvested in Nigeria?

Pineapple is usually harvested from November to April.

Which Nigerian states grow the most pineapple?

Edo, Ogun, Osun, Oyo, Delta, Cross River, Lagos and Kwara are among the best-known pineapple states.

Can I grow pineapple in my part of Nigeria?

Pineapple grows best in the South-West, South-South, South-East and North-Central regions. In other regions, ask your ADP extension officer before planting.

What diseases attack pineapple and how do I prevent them?

Mealybug wilt: Plant clean suckers and control the ants that carry mealybugs. Heart rot: Plant on well-drained land and avoid injuring plants.
